name: README.md
html:
luiskr.com V3 — star-field

Three.js star-field exploration experiment — the Solar System plus notable Milky Way, Local-Group and cosmic-hierarchy objects (Alpha/Proxima Centauri, Sirius, Vega, Betelgeuse, TRAPPIST-1, Sagittarius A*, the asteroid and Kuiper belts, Orion/Eagle/Crab/Helix nebulae, the Milky Way, Andromeda, Triangulum, the Local Group volume, superclusters and the observable-universe rim — 134 catalog bodies), each backed by a lazily-loaded JSON dossier of facts and deep-history notes from NASA/JPL, ESA, ESO and the IAU.

Every star is a system: authored point stars resolve into real photospheres (granulated spectral surfaces, sunspot activity, coronae, flares) on approach, with their actual planets and stellar companions orbiting — TRAPPIST-1 b–h, Tau Ceti e/f, Epsilon Eridani b, Barnard b, 51 Pegasi b, Kepler-452b, Sirius B, Capella Ab, Polaris Ab, Antares B — each a real pickable body with its own dossier in all 16 locales. From deep space they collapse back to the flat chart glyph, so the field reads correctly at every zoom.

Route: /star-field-experiment (canonical) with per-locale slugs for all 16 supported locales; reachable from the hamburger menu.

Submodule of luiskr.com-V3. Install deps from the superproject (yarn install at the root), then run yarn dev / yarn test / yarn build in this folder — see package.json scripts.

Layout

PathRole
StarField.tsx<view-star-field> — the route custom element: loader overlay, navigator drawer, dossier panel, hover HUD, keyboard/pointer handling.
starfield-engine.tsStarFieldEngine facade — owns the SFState bag and exposes the lifecycle surface (init, selectBody, flyHome, takeScreenshot, setReducedMotion).
star/Component layer — boot (engine bootstrap + loader/progress callbacks), render (JSX: loader, fallback field, navigator, dossier, HUD), i18n (label fetch + fallback), dossier (lazy locale:id-cached fetch).
engine/Three.js layer — bootstrap (lazy three import, WebGPU probe, textures, scene assembly, shader warmup), renderer-setup, scene (skybox + light rig + shared glow), bodies-scene (catalog → scene-graph dispatch), star-cloud (139k-record deep-field decode), registry (shard index) + registry-body (lazy registry spawn), fly (camera tween), picking, screenshot, state, scale (3-tier compression), materials (param hygiene), rand (seeded RNG), types, fallback-stars (painted 2D field for the no-WebGL path), fill-worker (wasm-pool dispatch for seeded buffer math), post + post-nodes (bloom/vignette/grain chain), catalog.ts (barrel), materials, spiral barrel.
engine/catalog/Body catalog split by region — solar (Sun/planets/moons/dwarfs/belts at diagram scale via shrinkSolar), milky-way (nearby systems at real galactic l/b/d), nebulae (+ globulars), galaxies (Milky Way disc + Andromeda + Triangulum), local-group (dwarf/satelite galaxies), hierarchy (cosmic boundary shells), geo (galactic→xyz + shrinkSolar).
engine/frame/Per-frame updates — camera (floating-origin pin + fly tween + hover-hint projection), updates (approach prefetch, distance LOD, shell/cloud fades, hover track), fx (pulse bodies, cycle tints, corona shimmer), shared (armed Vec3/Color workspace).
engine/spiral/Galaxy generation — fill (seeded point fields mirrored byte-for-byte in the WASM worker), galaxy (disc/sparkle/dust/core assembly).
engine/bodies/Body renderers — primitives (sphere/shell/halo material builders incl. sun-gated night-lights + fresnel atmosphere), deep-sky (photo billboards), mask (edge feather), belt (asteroid/Kuiper annuli), belt-rocks (hero displaced-polyhedron rocks), black-hole (Sgr A* composite), structures (hierarchy shells + member speckles), weather (living-planet: cloud deck, jet streams, hurricanes, aurorae, volcanism).
engine/bodies/procedural/Seeded canvas texture generators — corona, gas (nebula wisps), halo (annulus glow), star-surface (granulation + sunspots), surface (mottling/bands/craters), spikes (diffraction starburst), shared (paint primitives).
public/textures/Planet maps + skybox + nebula/galaxy photography.
public/data/<locale>/Per-locale dossiers — 134 bodies × 16 locales, fetched on approach/selection, cached per locale:id, English fallback.
public/data/index/139k-record registry — manifest + packed shards for search/browse.
public/media/Self-hosted NASA imagery/audio/video per body.
tests/Jest suites + tests/coverage/starfield/{component,engine,star} tails — 100% per-file gate.

Data model

engine/catalog/ is the sole body catalog (positions, radii, orbits, material recipes, groups), split by region into solar, milky-way, nebulae, galaxies, local-group and hierarchy, with geo owning the galactic-coordinate math; engine/catalog.ts is the barrel that re-exports them grouped. public/data/<locale>/<id>.json ships the display dossier (name, kind, tagline, facts[], history, source, media, meta provenance signature) — one file per body per locale so the viewer only downloads facts when the camera approaches or a body is selected, falling back to English when a locale file is absent. star/dossier.ts dedupes in-flight and resolved fetches in one shared locale:id cache.

public/data/index/ holds the deep-field registry — a manifest.json plus packed star-*/exoplanet-*/dso-* shards (139,563 records: 119,626 HYG/Hipparcos stars, 5,974 NASA Exoplanet Archive planets, 13,963 OpenNGC deep-sky objects). Records stream lazily for navigator search and per-kind "load more"; selecting a registry id materializes a real textured object at its true heliocentric position (engine/registry-body.ts) and synthesizes a dossier from the record fields instead of fetching JSON.

engine/scale.ts owns the chart scale: a continuous three-tier compression (galactic → Local Group → cosmic) that keeps close bodies at honest ratios while clamping the observable universe inside the scene. catalog.ts places every deep-sky body on its real galactic (l, b) direction through gpos; solar-neighborhood stars ride a legibility band (nbr) so Proxima doesn't collapse into the Sun.

Rendering

The engine runs on WebGPURenderer — all custom materials are TSL node materials (three/tsl + MeshBasicNodeMaterial), injected through SFNodeDeps from bootstrap.ts. Classic GLSL ShaderMaterial is not compatible with the node pipeline.

  • Solar bodies: texture-mapped spheres (MeshStandardMaterial under the sun rig) with per-body detail layers — Earth carries day, normal, night-emissive, specular, cloud-deck and elevation-bump maps.
  • Authored stars (near-LOD): a detail group swaps in on approach — granulated photosphere sphere (starSurfaceFor — convection-cell granulation + sunspot groups seeded by activity), annulus halo, corona sprite, and activity-seeded flare layers — replacing the flat far glyph. The flat point-sprite farGlyph shows at distance and hides when the detail group reveals (the inverse of the solar collapse).
  • Star systems: satellite lists are real parented SFBodyDefs — planets with authored eccentric orbits (TRAPPIST-1 b–h, τ Ceti e/f, ε Eri b, Barnard b, 51 Peg b, Kepler-452b) and stellar companions (Sirius B, Capella Ab, Polaris Ab, Antares B) — each pickable with its own dossier.
  • Earth day/night/seasons (engine/bodies/primitives.ts, engine/bodies-scene.ts, engine/frame/): the night-lights emissive is gated in-shader by dot(worldNormal, sunDir) through a MeshStandardNodeMaterial emissiveNode, so city lights only burn below the terminator and the day side stays clean; a fresnel-rim MeshBasicNodeMaterial shell tints the atmosphere day/dusk/night along the same shared sun vector. A counter-rotating lock group keeps the axial tilt inertially fixed while the orbit pivot spins, so the terminator sweeps real hemispheres over the year and the cycle surface tint keys off the orbital phase — a genuine four-seasons cycle instead of a wall-clock fade.
  • Luminous bodies (stars, the Sun, systems): a fresnel-limb node material blooms at the silhouette and dissolves into the halo instead of cutting a hard disc.
  • Saturn's ring: 2k_saturn_ring_alpha.png is a radial strip, so the ring geometry's planar UVs are remapped radius→U (bodies-scene.ts) to preserve the C/B/A bands and Cassini gap.
  • Living planets (engine/bodies/weather.ts): Earth and the wind-touched giants carry a procedural cloud deck — fbm coverage steered by the real 8k cloud map, latitude-banded differential rotation (jet streams), ITCZ convergence, hurricane vortices, polar snow advance/retreat, volcanic ash — plus the solar-wind cycle that drives flares and aurorae.
  • Nebulae/clusters: photographic billboards with a circular feather mask (engine/bodies/mask.ts) so square frames dissolve into space; procedural radial glows stand in when a photo is missing.
  • Galaxies: photo-textured tilted discs plus a sparkle-particle overlay and additive core glow (engine/spiral/); the seeded procedural particle disc remains as the fallback for unphotographed bodies.
  • Sagittarius A*: layered composite (engine/bodies/black-hole.ts) — black event horizon, thin photon ring, dust-lane accretion disc (TSL), orbiting plasma swirl, faint bipolar jets and a warm lensing-glow sprite.
  • Asteroid + Kuiper belts (engine/bodies/belt.ts, belt-rocks.ts): seeded particle annuli with Kirkwood gap lanes or a smooth classical disc, plus hero displaced-polyhedron rocks riding Keplerian pivots; raycast-disabled so pebbles never eat pointer hits.
  • Hierarchy structures (engine/bodies/structures.ts): fresnel-rim boundary shells (Local Group volume, superclusters, universe rim) with seeded member-galaxy speckle clouds; non-pickable by contract.
  • Orbit guides fade as they turn edge-on (frame/updates.ts updateRings) so a guide seen side-on dissolves instead of cutting a hard line.
  • All color textures are tagged SRGBColorSpace in bootstrap.ts.

Camera & navigation

  • Floating origin (frame/camera.ts followSelected): the followed body is pinned at the world origin by counter-translating a dedicated s.world group each frame — camera coordinates stay small, so float32 quantization can't jitter meshes when the galactic ride reaches millions of units.
  • Fly-to (engine/fly.ts): eased camera tween that resolves its target live inside the pinned frame — selecting a same-plane neighbour (Moon ↔ Earth, Jupiter ↔ moons) glides sideways instead of zooming out across the galactic span. Overview (flyHome) rides the Sun anchor so the solar system stays framed while it orbits.
  • Hover hints (starfield-engine.ts setHint, frame/camera.ts worldScreenPos): hovering/focusing a star-chart or registry row projects the target's world position to screen space and clamps it to the viewport edge with a leader line — the direction to the object is visible at any zoom, on- or off-screen.

Accessibility

One real <button> per body in the navigator drawer (full keyboard coverage), Escape dismisses the dossier panel first then the drawer, hover/selection announce through an aria-live region, and prefers-reduced-motion pauses the render loop. Pointer events unify mouse/touch/pen.

Assets

  • Planet/moon/sun maps + Saturn ring: Solar System Scope texture set, CC-BY 4.0.
  • Milky Way skybox: 8k equirect star panorama (same set).
  • Earth elevation bump map: NASA Visible Earth topography + bathymetry (public domain, via Wikimedia Commons Earth_dry_elevation.png).
  • Nebula/cluster/galaxy photography: NASA/ESA/ESO (Hubble/JWST/Chandra) and ESA Gaia mission imagery — public domain / CC-BY, hotlinked into public/textures/ at download time.
  • Face-on Milky Way map: ESA/Gaia all-sky artist impression.
  • Dossier media: self-hosted NASA/JPL imagery, audio and video under public/media/<body>/.
  • Dossier facts/history paraphrased from NASA/JPL Solar System Exploration, ESA, ESO and IAU publications — each JSON names its source and signs an acquisition/translation date in meta.

Commands

yarn dev      # mounts <view-star-field> directly
yarn test     # jest suite for star-field
yarn build    # emits experiments/star-field/dist/star-field.js
